KEY MESSAGE 1...Widespread rain today, possibly heavy at times. 
Watching for the potential for localized urban and poor-drainage 
flooding. 

Rain continues to overspread the region this morning and likely 
reaches the I-95 corridor by sunrise. Radar shows areas of heavier 
rainfall along and ahead of a warm front that will bring in a more 
moisture-rich higher theta-e airmass. Will see enough low level 
convergence for banded precipitation and areas of locally heavy 
rainfall through much of the day today. CAMs show that the greatest 
risk for heavy rains will be found across portions of central 
Massachusetts and Connecticut. Not entirely surprising given BUFKIT 
soundings depicting warm cloud depths increasing to 10-12k feet to 
the SW of the warm front. Notably, the HREF shows 10-30% probs of 
>1" of QPF in 3 hours in these same areas. Thus, this corridor will 
have the greatest risk for isolated urban/ poor drainage flooding. 
Further NE, cooler stratiform rain processes will be more dominant 
resulting in lighter rainfall rates. 

In terms of general rainfall totals, expecting a half an inch to an 
inch, with locally higher amounts of 1.5 to 3 inches SW of I-95. 
Further northeast, totals are in the range of a quarter to half an 
inch. Since these are showers versus stratiform rain, there could be 
areas of higher and lower amounts within a relatively short 
distance. Additionally, there's a lower chance for thunder, mainly 
Tuesday afternoon, with a few hundred J/kg of CAPE across mainly 
western Massachusetts and Connecticut, although it's not a 
significant risk.

Rain tapers off from W to E this afternoon, with drier conditions 
overspreading the region overnight. Guidance shows lingering areas 
of drizzle and light showers but this will be the exception and not 
the rule. Given extensive cloud cover, expect a much cooler day 
today, with highs mainly in the upper 60s to lower 70s. A true nod 
to the first day of meteorological fall.

KEY MESSAGE 2...Cloudy but drier on Wednesday with decreasing shower 
chances. Precipitation chances return Thursday with an increasing 
chance for showers and thunderstorms throughout the day.

1025 mb high pressure over the Maritimes should provide dry weather 
much of Wed, especially across eastern MA, while a frontal boundary 
lurks to the west and southwest of SNE. This front will eventually 
move northeast as a warm front later Wed and especially Wed night, 
resulting in an increased risk for showers and thunderstorms across 
SNE late Wed/Wed night. Cooler temps Wed, with 1025 Maritime high 
and ESE onshore flow, limiting max temps in the upper 60s and lower 
70s.

Greater risk for more widespread shower and thunderstorm activity 
Thursday as a short wave and surface cold front arrive from the 
west. Guidance is coming into better agreement with respect to 
increasing instability Thursday afternoon. The latest NBM shows 
widespread 60 to 80% probs of CAPE exceeding 1000 J/kg mainly along 
and S of the Mass Pike Thursday afternoon. These values are higher 
than previous runs so it is likely that guidance has trended north 
with the extent of the  warm sector over our CWA. Latest NSSL and 
CSU machine learning probabilistic guidance support these trends and 
highlight southern New England in a 15 percent chance for severe 
weather Thursday. Heat and humidity return Thu with warm sector 
airmass, highs in the lower 80s and dew pts in the upper 60s and 
lower 70s. 

KEY MESSAGE 3...Improving weather Friday and into the holiday 
weekend. Other than a spot diurnal shower each day, dry weather 
prevails with a mix of clouds and sun. Cooler than normal with highs 
in the 70s and lows in the 50s, along with onshore breezes.

Definitely a sign of fall approaching, with robust northern stream 
Friday yielding a baroclinic 998 mb maritime low late Fri/Sat. This 
will yield a cool, brisk NE flow into the SNE over the weekend. 
Highs likely remaining in the 70s and overnight lows in the 50s. It 
will feel even cooler over southeast MA, including Cape Cod and the 
Islands, with northeast winds 15-25 mph. Cool cyclonic flow aloft 
will yield diurnal clouds each day and possibly a spot shower. 
Otherwise, dry weather prevails. Possibly warmer and less wind for 
Memorial Day Monday, as high amplitude trough moves offshore and 
1025 mb high settles over SNE.
